title: Revenue by Order Status Using CASE Inside SUM
description:
For each month calculate the total revenue split by order status (completed, pending, cancelled) in separate columns using conditional aggregation.

**Table: orders** — `id`, `order_month`, `status`, `amount`

Output columns: `order_month`, `completed_revenue`, `pending_revenue`, `cancelled_revenue`. Order by `order_month`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, order_month VARCHAR, status VARCHAR, amount DECIMAL(10,2)); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,'2026-01','completed',200.00),(2,'2026-01','completed',300.00),(3,'2026-01','pending',150.00),(4,'2026-02','completed',450.00),(5,'2026-02','pending',100.00),(6,'2026-02','cancelled',80.00),(7,'2026-03','completed',600.00),(8,'2026-03','completed',250.00),(9,'2026-03','cancelled',120.00);
solution_sql: SELECT order_month, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'completed' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS completed_revenue, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'pending' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS pending_revenue, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_revenue FROM orders GROUP BY order_month ORDER BY order_month

test_cases.description: 9 orders across 3 months; each month collapses into 1 row with conditional sums — 3 rows total

hints: SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'X' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) acts as a conditional SUM — it adds amount only when the condition is met.
This is equivalent to a PIVOT and avoids multiple self-joins or subqueries.
explanation: CASE WHEN inside SUM acts as a filter within the aggregation. Jan: completed=500, pending=150, cancelled=0. Feb: completed=450, pending=100, cancelled=80. Mar: completed=850, pending=0, cancelled=120. GROUP BY order_month collapses the 9 input rows into 3 output rows. Using ELSE 0 ensures NULL is not produced for missing statuses.
